publications.title: LEGOS-SLEEC: Tool for Formalizing and Analyzing Normative Requirements
publications.subtitle: 2025 International Conference on Software Engineering
publications.description: Systems interacting with humans, such as assistive robots or chatbots, are increasingly integrated into our society. To prevent these systems from causing social, legal, ethical, empathetic, or cultural (SLEEC) harms, normative requirements specify the permissible range of their behaviors. These requirements encompass both functional and non-functional aspects and are defined with respect to time. Typically, these requirements are specified by stakeholders from a broad range of fields, such as lawyers, ethicists, or philosophers, who may lack technical expertise. Because such stakeholders often have different goals, responsibilities, and objectives, ensuring that these requirements are well-formed is crucial. SLEEC DSL, a domain-specific language resembling natural language, has been developed to formalize these requirements as SLEEC rules. In this paper, we present LEGOS-SLEEC, a tool designed to support interdisciplinary stakeholders in specifying normative requirements as SLEEC rules, and in analyzing and debugging their well-formedness. LEGOS-SLEEC is built using four previously published components, which have been shown to be effective and usable across nine case studies. Reflecting on this experience, we have significantly improved the user interface of LEGOS-SLEEC and its diagnostic support, and demonstrate the effectiveness of these improvements using four interdisciplinary stakeholders

projects.title: SLEEC IntelliJ Plugin
projects.description: Developed an IntelliJ plugin for the Sleec language, designed to support interdisciplinary teams in specifying normative requirements. The plugin features custom parsing, syntax highlighting, dynamic code completion, and an interactive tool window for analyzing rules and concerns. It bridges technical and non-technical domains, enhancing accessibility and productivity, and was showcased in an academic publication.

Last week I had a great time at UofTHacks 13 where I built NowAndThen with my team: Nathan Espejo , Alyssa Hee , and Vicheka Oeun . They were a huge part of this and I genuinely could not have done it without them. We built a mobile app NowAndThen that lets people leave comments, photos, and videos tied to a specific place, then explore nearby memories and replay trails through space and time. It also includes friends, likes, and an AI summary that captures the identity of a location. We used React Native, Node + Express, and MongoDB. Huge thank you to the sponsors for making the event possible, and a special thanks to Brent Wolfram for taking the time for a great coffee chat. Big thank you as well to the organizers and judges for putting on an awesome event! ...more

Wrapped up a weekend of hacking at Hack the North 2025! We built Mentral AI, a VS Code extension that learns a mentor's style from GitHub and gives code review feedback in that voice. Under the hood, we paired a lightweight analysis engine with AST signals and a compact RAG setup on Gemini, with VAPI handling voice and made it to the final round with Warp! (Without these guys, none of it would have happened Jasiri Wa-Kyendo, Jaskirat Gill , Ekansh Chawla )! Learn more about the project below: DevPost: https://lnkd.in/dbag96kE #HTN2025 #HackTheNorth # ...more
